output.summary: KEP-4872 proposes that the kube-apiserver validate that a kubelet serving certificate's Common Name equals system:node:<nodename> when connecting to kubelets, to stop a node from impersonating another node using a certificate for a reused IP. Its status is implementable at alpha stage; the sources show it was revised to be opt-in via a new CLI flag.
output.rationale: Cloud IPs get reassigned faster than kubelet serving certificates expire, so a certificate issued to an old node can be used for a new node sharing that IP. The proposal adds CN validation in the kube-apiserver, which already knows the target node name when it connects for logs, exec, and port-forward. Reviewers asked for opt-in behavior so that existing configurations see no default change.

alternatives.option: Keep validation on by default behind a feature gate only
alternatives.why_not: enj asked for the feature to be opt-in: "The default today is no TLS verification at all so it does not make sense for us to tighten this in a way that will just cause upgrade failures."

alternatives.option: Per-node client-go transports for the custom CN check
alternatives.why_not: liggitt warned it would leak transports: "This approach looks like it will make a new transport per node, which gets held forever in the transport tlsCache"
Suggested by sftim as a naming alternative in review; the sources do not record it being adopted.

evidence.quote: We propose that the Kube API server is modified to validate the Common Name (CN) of the kubelet's serving certificate to be equal to
Invert this and make it opt-in via a new flag that must be set in addition to `--kubelet-certificate-authority`.
Okay, let's go with requiring opt-in so there are no default behavior changes and we are fully backwards compatible with any existing configuration.
